title: Porchetta
subtitle: Herb-stuffed slow-roasted pork belly
excerpt: Porchetta is a whole rolled pork belly stuffed with garlic, rosemary, fennel seeds, and sage, then roasted slowly until the flesh is juicy and the crackling is blistered and crisp. The home version is made with a pork belly joint, scored and seasoned the night before. It serves a crowd and is excellent cold the next day.
sourceNotes: Central Italian regional recipe, most associated with Lazio and Umbria. Porchetta is documented across Italian culinary sources. Method drawn from traditional porchetta-roasting techniques and Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking (1992).

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice and freeze. Thaw overnight. Eat cold or very gently warmed.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Score and season the pork 8 to 24 hours ahead and leave uncovered in the fridge for dry crackling.
recipe.temperatureNote: start high to blister the skin, then reduce to 160°C

glossaryTerms.definition: The blistered, crispy pork skin produced by scoring the fat, drying the skin, and roasting it at high heat; the contrast with the soft meat below is the point of a good porchetta.

content.text: Porchetta is a rolled pork belly seasoned with garlic, rosemary, fennel seeds, and sage, then roasted over several hours until the flesh is soft and the skin has become proper
. The key to the crackling is dry skin: score it, salt it, and leave it uncovered in the fridge overnight. The key to the meat is low heat and a long oven time after the initial blast.

items.prepNote: skin-on, boned, butterflied open by butcher if possible

content.text: Score the pork skin in a close crosshatch, 1 cm apart, cutting through the fat but not into the meat. Mix the garlic, rosemary, sage, fennel seeds, black pepper, chilli if using, and {{olive-oil}} of olive oil into a paste. Spread all over the flesh side of the pork.
Roll the pork tightly, skin-side out, and tie at 3 cm intervals with kitchen twine. Rub the skin with salt. Place on a rack in the fridge, uncovered, for 8 to 24 hours.
Take the pork out of the fridge 1 hour before roasting. Heat the oven to 220°C. Roast the pork on a rack over a roasting tin for 30 minutes until the skin has blistered and begun to colour.
Reduce the heat to 160°C. Roast for a further 2.5 hours (about 45 minutes per 500 g of meat weight). The internal temperature should reach 75°C. Rest for 20 minutes before carving.

items.cause: Not dry enough before roasting, or the temperature was not high enough at the start.
items.fix: Dry overnight is non-negotiable. If the skin is soft after the initial 30 minutes at 220°C, increase the heat to 240°C for the final 20 minutes.

items.cause: Too much filling, or the roll was not tight enough.
items.fix: Leave a 2 cm border when spreading the filling. Roll tightly and tie before the filling can shift.

content.text: Porchetta is central Italian street food, associated above all with the towns around Ariccia in the Castelli Romani near Rome. It is sold from large vans and market stalls, sliced thickly into rolls. The home version, made for a large gathering, follows exactly the same principles: the herbs, the slow cook, and the crackling. Cold porchetta the next day, sliced thin and eaten in a roll, is considered by many to be even better than the hot version.
